To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an end-to end system for automatic scoring of spoken responses to a neuropsychological narrative recall test, which is a key test for screening for mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

1) we can use automatic speech recognition to extract features from a spoken recall test that are comparable to those used in manual clinical assessment, 2) we can use those features to classify the subjects as cognitively impaired or not, and 3) the resulting classification accuracy is comparable to that of the clinical assessment.
we present an end-toend system for automatically scoring narrative recall tests administered to seniors when detecting cognitive impairment.

automatic assessment of narrative recall tests is possible and that ASR errors are not a major factor in the accuracy of automatic assessment.
